acceptance_criteria.criterion: A bare slug that exists in exactly one repo namespace returns the correct storage path
A bare slug that exists in two or more repo namespaces throws an AMBIGUOUS error that lists all matching qualified paths
Each segment of a qualified input is individually validated against assertSafeSlug (repo and slug validated separately — no composite string)

summary: Added resolveProjectDir(slugOrQualified, ledgerRoot): Promise<string> to mcp-server/src/utils/ledger-root.ts. Qualified {repo}/{slug} input validates each segment individually via local assertSafeSlug (uses SAFE_SLUG_REGEX — stricter than the loose guard in run-log-handlers.ts) and returns join(ledgerRoot, repo, slug) with no filesystem access. Bare-slug input scans all non-dot repo-namespace subdirectories of ledgerRoot using readdir, collects matches, returns the path if exactly one match exists, throws AMBIGUOUS (listing all qualified paths) on multiple matches, or throws NOT_FOUND if no match. Added readdir import to ledger-root.ts. Created mcp-server/tests/storage/slug-resolution.test.ts with 17 tests covering all 4 acceptance criteria plus NOT_FOUND and dot-prefix skip cases. All 17 tests pass; tsc --noEmit clean; pre-existing GUI test failures are unrelated to this WP.

comments.note: assertSafeSlug in ledger-root.ts is stricter than the homonymous local function in run-log-handlers.ts (which only checks includes('/') and includes('..')). When Phase 3 WPs update the GUI handlers, consider extracting the strict SAFE_SLUG_REGEX-based assertSafeSlug to a shared utility (e.g., path-validator.ts) to avoid divergence between the two guards.

resolveProjectDir uses readdir() to probe candidate directories, which issues one syscall per namespace directory. For ledger roots with many namespaces this is linear. The current usage pattern (called only on GUI handler request paths) makes this acceptable, but a stat()-based probe would be slightly more efficient for existence checks without needing to enumerate directory entries.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (ledger-root.ts, slug-resolution.test.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info. Security sign-off: PASS. The qualified-path branch is secure — SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) blocks all path-traversal inputs including '..', '/', backslash, null bytes, and Unicode. The bare-slug branch has a Medium gap: the slug is not validated via assertSafeSlug before the filesystem probe, allowing inputs like '..' that are bounded within ledgerRoot but return incorrect paths. No Critical or High findings; implementation is safe for current additive state (function not yet wired to any handler).

comments.note: A04 — Insecure Design: bare-slug branch (lines 162–197 of ledger-root.ts) never calls assertSafeSlug on the slug before the filesystem probe. A bare input of '..' (no slash) enters the bare-slug path; join(ledgerRoot, namespace, '..') normalises to ledgerRoot and readdir(ledgerRoot) succeeds, causing '..' to match every existing namespace. Traversal is bounded — cannot escape ledgerRoot — but the function may return ledgerRoot as the resolved project path rather than rejecting the input. Recommended fix: add assertSafeSlug(slug) as the first statement in the bare-slug branch (after the includes('/') check), before any filesystem access. This is consistent with how qualified-path segments are validated.

A09 — Information Disclosure via error messages: the NOT_FOUND error (line 193 of ledger-root.ts) embeds the absolute ledgerRoot path: "NOT_FOUND: project slug '...' was not found in any repo namespace under '/absolute/path/to/ledger'". When resolveProjectDir is wired to a GUI/API handler, this message should be sanitised before returning to callers — strip the filesystem path from the user-facing message and retain it only in server-side logs. The AMBIGUOUS error is safe (it contains only repo/slug strings, not filesystem paths).

Info — Duplicate assertSafeSlug implementations: ledger-root.ts (line 122) and run-log-handlers.ts (line 43) each define a local assertSafeSlug with identical SAFE_SLUG_REGEX logic. This was already flagged in the implementation pipeline. Before resolveProjectDir is consumed by any handler, extract the shared guard to a common utility (e.g. src/utils/path-validator.ts) to avoid future divergence.
